title: dslim/bert-base-NER, actually measured against EXP-033's rule-tagger-vs-spaCy comparison
goal: Pick up EXP-033's own named follow-up: measure dslim/bert-base-NER (loaded in lab.common.real_encoders since EXP-033/034's era, never actually called for entity detection until now) on the identical gold fixture, for a real three-way comparison against the rule tagger and the spaCy substitute.
method: The same 12 hand-labeled sentences / 19 PERSON-ORG spans EXP-033 used (imported directly from that exploration's GOLD, not re-picked), scored the identical way (text-containment hit counting, micro-averaged precision/recall/F1) against lab.common.real_ner.detect_real, the new wiring of the dslim/bert-base-NER pipeline already loaded in lab.common.real_encoders.

real_model_card.gliner_reason: the `gliner` package is not installed in this environment; dslim/bert-base-NER is the real checkpoint measured for the NER role instead

results_prose: On the identical EXP-033 fixture (12 sentences, 19 gold PERSON/ORG spans): rule tagger F1 0.7059 (unchanged from EXP-008/033, measured again here as the baseline). dslim/bert-base-NER F1 0.8085 (precision 0.6786, recall 1.0) -- the first real measurement of this checkpoint anywhere in this repo. spaCy en_core_web_sm (EXP-033): F1 0.7619, for reference, not rerun here.
conclusion: dslim/bert-base-NER, the actual blueprint-named checkpoint, outperforms both the rule tagger and the spaCy substitute EXP-033 used when HuggingFace was unreachable -- a real, direct three-way comparison, not an assumption that the originally-intended checkpoint would be better just because it's the one the blueprint named. EXP-033/034's gap is closed: the checkpoint was loaded but never actually called for this role until now.
scale_down: Same 12-sentence fixture as EXP-033 -- not a held-out annotated corpus, chosen for a direct, controlled comparison against an already-measured result rather than a fresh, larger evaluation.
follow_ups: Hand-label a larger gold sentence set (50+, matching EXP-008's own scale) for a more stable F1 estimate across all three taggers.

lab.common.real_ner.detect_real only maps PER/ORG -- dslim/bert-base-NER's LOC/MISC categories are dropped rather than mapped to this project's address/date/amount labels, which it was never trained to produce; address detection still depends entirely on the regex tagger.

Not yet wired into lab.common.brain.reason's identity-extraction step (detect_primary is still what that step calls) -- this measures the checkpoint standalone, matching EXP-033's own scope, not a live pipeline swap.
models_used: dslim/bert-base-NER (CoNLL-2003 token classifier, non-generative), via lab.common.real_encoders.real_entities, wired through lab.common.real_ner. No generative model.
